harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created the opsbot account on node1 and node2 (RHEL 7), generated an ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1, installed the public key into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2, and locked the opsbot password on both nodes. Added a `Match User opsbot { PasswordAuthentication no; PubkeyAuthentication yes }` block to /etc/ssh/sshd_config on both nodes (the pre-existing global `PasswordAuthentication no` at the bottom of the file was actually a no-op since OpenSSH honors only the first occurrence of a keyword in the global context, which was `yes`). Verified opsbot@node1 can SSH to opsbot@node2 using the key with no password prompt, and that password-only auth attempts for opsbot are rejected on both nodes (server offers only publickey/gssapi). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes: captured boot_id baselines, rebooted node1 then polled until reachable with a new boot_id, verified sshd/opsbot/keys/cross-node SSH recovered, then repeated for node2, and re-verified password auth is still rejected post-reboot on both nodes.
actions_performed: Inspected OS/sudo access on node1 and node2 (RHEL 7.9)
Created opsbot user on node1 and node2 via useradd -m
Locked opsbot password (passwd -l) on both nodes
Generated ed25519 SSH keypair for opsbot on node1
Installed node1 opsbot public key into node2's opsbot authorized_keys with correct ownership/permissions
Diagnosed sshd_config first-match-wins semantics showing global PasswordAuthentication was effectively 'yes'
Added Match User opsbot block (PasswordAuthentication no, PubkeyAuthentication yes) to sshd_config on both nodes
Validated config with sshd -t and reloaded sshd on both nodes
Verified key-based SSH from node1 opsbot to node2 opsbot succeeds
Verified password-only auth is rejected for opsbot on both nodes
Captured boot_id/service/data baseline on both nodes
Rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until back, verified new boot_id, sshd active, opsbot/key intact, cross-node SSH still works
Rebooted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until back, verified new boot_id, sshd active, opsbot/authorized_keys intact
Re-verified cross-node key SSH and password-auth rejection on both nodes post-reboot

evidence.requirement: opsbot account created on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: useradd succeeded on both nodes; id opsbot shows uid=1001(opsbot) on each

evidence.requirement: SSH keypair generated on node1 and public key installed on node2 for opsbot
evidence.summary: ed25519 keypair generated for opsbot on node1; matching public key present in node2's /home/opsbot/.ssh/authorized_keys with 600 perms

evidence.requirement: opsbot can run commands on node2 via key-based SSH from node1
evidence.summary: BatchMode SSH from opsbot@node1 to opsbot@node2 using the private key succeeded, returning whoami/hostname/id from node2

evidence.requirement: Key-based authentication required (password auth rejected) for opsbot on node1
evidence.summary: SSH attempt with PubkeyAuthentication disabled and password-only preferred auth against node1 returned 'Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic)'

evidence.requirement: Key-based authentication required (password auth rejected) for opsbot on node2
evidence.summary: Same password-only SSH attempt against node2 was rejected identically, confirming no password auth path

evidence.requirement: sshd config change was valid and applied on both nodes
evidence.summary: sshd -t passed after adding Match User opsbot block on both nodes; sshd reloaded and reported active on both

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node1 boot_id 0d6209e2-350d-4cd9-8a7d-11f7c08072be, sshd active, opsbot present, private key file present

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot on node1 acknowledged (connection closed); after polling, node1 came back with new boot_id 6faf973e-bfe9-4cea-958c-6ba63fc82f99, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services/data and cross-node SSH
evidence.summary: Post-reboot node1: sshd active, opsbot account and key intact, and opsbot@node1 successfully SSH'd to opsbot@node2 using the key

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node2 boot_id 2fc81aed-3ce8-4a35-8f4c-b73206afa45f, sshd active, opsbot present, authorized_keys present

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot on node2 acknowledged (connection closed); after polling, node2 came back with new boot_id 0e79c01b-84f3-4b69-af0a-c2c13e6f206b, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery of required services/data and cross-node SSH
evidence.summary: Post-reboot node2: sshd active, opsbot account and authorized_keys intact with correct public key content; opsbot@node1 successfully SSH'd into node2 post-reboot

evidence.requirement: Password auth still rejected for opsbot on both nodes after restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot password-only SSH attempts against opsbot on node1 and node2 were both rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic)', confirming key-only auth persisted across restart
